claims.text: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi and closely related high-entropy derivatives have coercive fields no greater than 100 Oe under conventional processing.
Single-phase fcc FeCoNi has high saturation magnetization.
Adding approximately 3–5 at% Al and aging near 550°C for several hours will induce nanoscale L12-ordered precipitates in the fcc matrix.
The induced L12 precipitates will be coherent with the fcc matrix.
The L12 precipitates produce lattice misfit and localized strain fields.
The L12 precipitates and their strain fields act as pinning sites for magnetic domain walls.
Enhanced domain-wall pinning raises the energy barrier for magnetization reversal.
The increased reversal barrier will increase coercivity.
The proposed treatment will raise coercivity well above approximately 100 Oe.
The treated alloy is predicted to exhibit an approximately 50% or greater coercivity increase relative to the control.
The treated alloy is predicted to retain high saturation magnetization.
An inert atmosphere will prevent oxidation during aging.
The selected aging conditions provide enough diffusion for L12 precipitation without causing unwanted grain growth or precipitate coarsening.
The proposed mechanism applies only where coherent L12 precipitation is thermodynamically and kinetically accessible.
Room-temperature VSM hysteresis measurements can be used to compare coercive fields of aged baseline and Al-modified samples.
A coercivity increase of no more than 20%, or failure to detect coherent L12 precipitates, is defined as falsifying the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The headline prediction requires coercivity well above 100 Oe and suggests an approximately 50% increase, whereas the falsification rule would accept any statistically significant increase greater than 20%. A sample starting well below 100 Oe could pass the stated test while remaining below 100 Oe and falling far short of the headline prediction.
